name: とんかつの菊屋 (Tonkatsu no Kikuya)

claims.text: All cutlets are breaded in wheat-flour panko and deep-fried in shared frying oil, so cross-contamination with gluten is unavoidable.
Tonkatsu sauce and standard soy-based seasonings used here are wheat-containing; no wheat-free sauce alternative is documented.
The kitchen centers on deep-fried pork and chicken and pork-based soup, so all preparation involves animal products with no separate vegan handling noted.

name: とんかつ料理 さち (Tonkatsu Ryori Sachi)

claims.text: All cutlets are breaded in wheat flour and panko and deep-fried, so the fryer and core dishes contain gluten; no gluten-free handling is documented.
The house dipping sauce is a secret soy-sauce/Worcestershire-style tare mixed with grated daikon, which typically contains wheat.
Menu is entirely pork-cutlet based; no vegan or vegetarian options are documented.

name: とんかつ とんき (Tonkatsu Tonki)

claims.text: All cutlets are coated in wheat flour and panko and deep-fried, so the shared fryers carry gluten; no gluten-free preparation is indicated.
House tonkatsu sauce is used on the cutlets; tonkatsu sauce is wheat-based and not gluten-free.
Frying oil is 100% lard (pork fat), so all fried items are cooked in animal fat; the set also includes pork soup.

Signature fried oysters use wheat-flour batter and breadcrumbs, and the kitchen also serves udon, soba, and ramen, so the shared fry oil and prep surfaces present a high gluten cross-contamination risk.
Grilled and simmered seafood and donburi are glazed/seasoned with standard Japanese soy sauce, which normally contains wheat; no wheat-free tamari is documented.
The menu is seafood-centered (oysters, anago) with egg-based chawanmushi and dashi/soy seasoning throughout, so there is no separation from animal ingredients.
The affiliated company's site states food-allergy inquiries can be accommodated, but no celiac- or vegan-specific protocol is documented for the dining hall.
Savory island dishes such as anago-don and oyster dishes are served with standard Japanese seasonings, which typically include wheat-based soy sauce.
Menu is built around wheat (sandwiches/bread, pasta, lunch plates) with no documented gluten-free handling; high cross-contamination risk for celiac diners.
Food items center on egg, dairy, meat and fish (egg sandwiches, grilled-meat lunches, salmon/tarako pasta); no separate vegan preparation is documented.
The shop's entire core product line is wheat-flour sponge cake baked on the premises, so the environment is flour-heavy with no gluten-free preparation noted.

Manju are baked with batter and offered alongside milk chocolate and dairy items, with the seasonal oyster gratin bun containing shellfish and cream sauce, indicating shared handling of animal-derived ingredients.
Momiji manju are hand-made and baked in-shop, and can be eaten fresh in a small seating area.
The entire menu is built around oysters (shellfish); creative dishes such as gratin also use dairy, so there is no separation from animal products.
